meta_title: Photographers and videographers — The Lord of the Rings 2026
description: Photographers and videographers at The Lord of the Rings: costume duty, rules of movement during the game, drones, use of photos and video, how to arrange things with the organisers.
title: Photographers and videographers
subtitle: Capture the story, but don’t step into it.
intro_lead: Want to capture the battle, the camp, the costumes and the atmosphere of Middle-earth? Excellent. You just need to know how to move around the event safely, how not to disrupt play and how to respect others.
who_intro: This page is for people who want to take photos or shoot video at the event:
who_l3: as members of groups who want to document their army,
who_l4: as participants who want to create content from the backstage, the camp or the programme.
who_note: Photographers and videographers are welcome, but they must respect safety, the rules, the privacy of participants and the atmosphere of the game.
h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
s60_l1_strong: the same costume duty as other participants
s60_l2_pre: If you really can’t have a full costume, at least dress
s60_l2_strong: unobtrusively, in dark, natural and non-distracting tones
s60_l3: If you’re not sure, arrange it with the organisers in advance — we’ll help with borrowing suitable clothes or covering up modern items.
s60_l4_strong: if you don’t look like you’re from Middle-earth, stay out of other people’s shots
s60_l5: Safety matters more than the shot.
s60_l6: Don’t enter the combat line, don’t step among weapons, retreating armies or anywhere players can’t safely perceive you.
s60_l7: Respect the instructions of organisers, commanders and medics.
s60_l8: Be especially careful with children, sensitive situations and injuries.
cost_p1: The Lord of the Rings stands on the atmosphere of Middle-earth. Everyone who moves in the play space, in the camp and near players helps create that atmosphere — or can accidentally break it.
cost_alert_strong: Photographers and videographers have a costume duty just like everyone else.
cost_alert_post: You don’t need heavy armour or a perfect costume, but you should look such that you can appear in other people’s shots without being a distraction.
cos_l1: a cloak, tunic, shirt, scarf, simple period or fantasy top,
cos_l5: a bag or case without bright modern colours,
cos_l6: as few reflective elements and logos as possible.
h_no_costume: When you don’t have a costume
no_p1: Write to us in advance. We’ll try to advise what can be put together easily, or whether something can be borrowed or covered up on site.
no_p2: If you turn up at the event in modern, bright or distracting clothes, you can only shoot away from in-game shots and away from places where you’d step into the atmosphere of others.
h_what: What you can photograph and film
yes_l5: the atmosphere of the evening camp,
yes_l6: stalls, crafts, the inn and the community,
yes_l7: the Saturday main game from a safe distance,
yes_l8: the children’s game only carefully and with respect for parents and the organiser’s rules.
no_l4: children without a reasonable context and consent,
no_l5: situations that could embarrass or harm someone.
move_l3: don’t stand behind a player who is retreating,
move_l4: don’t step into places where players are hit and fall,
move_l5: don’t approach archers in a way that prevents them from safely seeing you,
move_l6: if an organiser says “away”, you go away immediately.
move_note: A good photo isn’t worth an injury.
rule_alert_strong: If you don’t look like you’re from Middle-earth, stay out of other people’s shots.
rule_l1: don’t walk in front of other photographers and videographers in modern clothes,
rule_l2: don’t stand in the background of hero scenes, line-ups and atmospheric shots,
rule_l3: don’t get in the way during staged army photos,
rule_l4: if you know you don’t fit in visually, stay out of the main frame.
use_intro: If you’re creating public content, follow these principles:
use_l1: state that this is The Lord of the Rings / Moravian LARP event,
use_l2: where possible, tag the official event profiles,
use_l3: don’t edit photos to mock or harm anyone,
use_l4: don’t use shots of children, injuries or sensitive situations without consent,
use_l5: if someone asks you to take down a specific photo, handle it politely and quickly.
exp_l1: A pre-arrangement if you want to be an official photographer or videographer.
exp_l2: Respect for the rules and instructions of the organisers.
exp_l3: A costume, or at least non-distracting clothes.
exp_l4: Consideration for players, children, parents and stallholders.
exp_l5: A clear arrangement on whether you’re shooting for yourself, for the group, for media or for the organisers.
reg_p1: If you’re coming as a regular participant and shooting for yourself, the standard registration is enough.
reg_l2: move closer than regular participants during play,
reg_p3_pre: write to us in advance at
reg_alert_post: and similar equipment are only allowed after prior arrangement with the organisers and with regard to safety, privacy and the venue.

cta_heading: Want to photograph or film The Lord of the Rings?
cta_body: Write to us about your plan and how you stand on the costume side. We’ll arrange where you can move, which shots make sense and how to get a nice output without disrupting the game.
